# ledger_bucket (Resource)

A Ledger bucket: a user-defined grouping of commitments and accounts used to slice the monthly outlook. A bucket never holds, allocates or reserves money and is not a budget envelope. Names are unique ignoring case, archived buckets included.

Import with the identifier: `terraform import ledger_bucket.example <id>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A bucket groups commitments and accounts to slice the monthly outlook. It holds no money and is not a budget envelope.
resource "ledger_bucket" "fixed_costs" {
  name = "Fixed costs"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name, 1 to 80 characters. Ledger trims names and collapses white space, so write it that way. Renaming keeps the identifier and therefore every assignment.

### Optional

- `archived` (Boolean) Whether the bucket is archived. Archiving keeps the bucket and every assignment to it (history stays readable) and stops anything new from using it. Archive instead of destroying when anything is assigned. Defaults to `false`.
- `reassign_to` (String) Used only when this resource is destroyed: the identifier of an active bucket that existing assignments move to. Without it, destroying a bucket that is still assigned fails with `definition_in_use`. The assignments become the person's own (origin user). Not read back from Ledger, so it is empty after an import.

### Read-Only

- `archived_at` (String) When it was archived (RFC 3339, UTC), or null.
- `created_at` (String) When it was created (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `id` (String) The Ledger identifier (a ULID). It never changes, so a rename reaches every assignment.
- `updated_at` (String) When it last changed (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `version` (Number) The optimistic-concurrency version (the ETag). Changes are sent against the version Terraform last read; a stale one fails instead of overwriting.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import ledger_bucket.fixed_costs 01JD3Y4C8V9M2Q7W5R6T0XZBNA
```
